evals.prompt: Install @stdiobus/skills in this npm consumer and connect it to our existing MCP host. We need reproducible launch configuration.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the consumer and registry, preserve its manager/lockfile, select and pin the requested compatible release, and verify the configured route.
assertions: Records the actual npm package version separately from the handshake version.
Uses the executable bin or resolved mcp-server export, with separate command and args.
Does not require building this repository for an installed release.

evals.prompt: I installed @stdiobus/skills@1.1.1, but read_skill rejects evidence-driven-rd. Make the agent able to find the right instructions without silently changing my package version.
evals.expected_output: Discover the running catalog, identify the stable/RC capability gap, and explain available authorized options without pretending the missing skill exists.
assertions: Checks list_skills on the running connection.
Identifies that the checked 1.1.1 does not contain evidence-driven-rd.
Does not silently switch to RC or patch node_modules.

evals.prompt: read_reference works but require.resolve for @stdiobus/skills/skills/runtime-patterns-http/references/templates/single-get.ts throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED in 1.1.1.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the installed export map and use verified MCP reading or an explicitly version-specific physical file fallback.
assertions: Distinguishes the stable two-wildcard export defect from a missing reference file.
Uses a listed MCP resource path without the references/ prefix.
Does not import the template as JavaScript.

evals.prompt: let the agent read the correct packaged template; the worker is already connected and I do not want another server process
evals.expected_output: Reuse the existing MCP connection, discover a suitable skill, read it, list resources, and load only the relevant template.
assertions: Reuses the existing connection.
Reads SKILL.md before selecting conditional resources.
Checks isError and decodes only JSON-returning tools as JSON.

evals.prompt: Our stdio Bus application needs @stdiobus/skills as a worker. Show and verify the installed-package route, not a path into your checkout.
evals.expected_output: Use the existing StdioBus pool and installed executable resolution; preserve connection ownership and verify requests through the bus.
assertions: Resolves @stdiobus/skills/mcp-server from the consumer.
Keeps initialization and tool calls on the same worker/session.
Uses stop and destroy only for an owned bus.
Does not claim a direct subprocess test proves the bus route.

evals.prompt: Can I import createFileResolver and instantiate Skill from @stdiobus/skills? I need to read files in my ESM app.
evals.expected_output: Explain the actual public exports and use filesystem reads of resolved exported paths.
assertions: Identifies SkillName as the runtime enum and Skill/SkillManifest as TypeScript-only types.
Does not invent createFileResolver as a public export.
Uses ESM and createRequire resolution for text files.

evals.prompt: tools/list shows five tools. How do I search for an applicable skill and load just the references I need?
evals.expected_output: Follow discovery, lexical search, applicability checks, explicit skill loading, and conditional resource reads.
assertions: Names all five existing tools with their real argument shapes.
Does not describe search as embeddings or semantic retrieval.
Preserves the exact listed reference path.

evals.prompt: The @stdiobus/skills handshake says 1.0.0, but npm says 1.2.0-rc.0. Is the wrong server running?
evals.expected_output: Compare package identity and manifest identity before diagnosing a mismatch.
assertions: Explains that serverInfo.version comes from manifest.version.
Reads installed package.json to determine the npm version.
Does not infer a wrong binary solely from those different versions.

evals.prompt: verify this installed skills pakage end to end; no mocks, no publishing, and do not execute any retrieved scripts
evals.expected_output: Run real installed-package delivery checks and report their limits.
assertions: Uses the helper or equivalent real MCP calls against the specified installation.
Compares returned skill and resource text with installed files.
Reports direct export gaps separately from MCP delivery.
Does not claim measured LLM behavior or execute resource scripts.

evals.prompt: After searching in Russian I got an empty result. Does the @stdiobus/skills package have no relevant skill?
evals.expected_output: Inspect the catalog and retry concrete English lexical terms without overstating absence.
assertions: Explains ASCII tokenization and lack of automatic translation.
Uses list_skills as the authoritative available-name list.
Does not treat a zero score or empty list as proof of subject absence.

evals.prompt: Create a new Agent Skill for our incident review process using agent-skills/create-skill.
evals.expected_output: Use the repository create-skill workflow; package-consumer instructions are not needed.
assertions: Does not activate this package-consumption skill solely to author a skill.

evals.prompt: Continue our empirical R&D and test whether the candidate filter actually speeds up our real workload.
evals.expected_output: Use evidence-driven-rd for the investigation, without unsolicited npm setup.
assertions: Does not substitute package installation or MCP delivery checks for the requested experiment.

evals.prompt: Build a Node.js stdio Bus worker pool for my own JSON-RPC image converter; it does not consume @stdiobus/skills.
evals.expected_output: Use stdiobus-sdk-node or the converter project contracts.
assertions: Does not activate this skill merely because stdio Bus and workers are mentioned.

evals.prompt: Implement a new MCP server with an HTTP transport and a write_document tool. This is unrelated to the skills package.
evals.expected_output: Use the target server project architecture, not this read-only consumer procedure.
assertions: Does not impose this package's five-tool contract on a different server.

evals.prompt: npm install fails in my unrelated React application. Explain the package-lock conflict.
evals.expected_output: Handle the React dependency issue without loading this package-specific skill.
assertions: Does not install or inspect @stdiobus/skills.

evals.prompt: Publish the next @stdiobus/skills release and move its npm dist-tag after review.
evals.expected_output: Follow the explicitly authorized release procedure; this skill is scoped to consumption, not release management.
assertions: Does not activate the consumer skill as a substitute for release requirements.

evals.prompt: Translate the sentence "read the packaged skill" into French. Do not inspect any files.
evals.expected_output: Translate the sentence only.
assertions: Does not invoke MCP tools, npm commands, or package verification.

evals.prompt: Add a dynamic provider-admission feature to the @stdiobus/skills server architecture.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the repository and design the requested server extension under its existing contracts.
assertions: Does not activate this consumer skill as an implementation specification for a new provider system.

evals.prompt: Using a framework skill already loaded, implement an SQS handler in my Runtime Web application. No package setup is needed.
evals.expected_output: Use runtime-patterns-async and the application contracts.
assertions: Does not perform unsolicited skills-server installation or consumer verification.

evals.prompt: Correct spelling in this paragraph about @stdiobus/skills without verifying its technical content.
evals.expected_output: Perform the requested bounded prose edit only.
assertions: Does not activate package-consumption procedures for a spelling-only task.
